context: Sets out municipal population, municipal taxes and average burden per household for Japanese, Koreans and foreigners, to show that the Koreans, though more numerous, bear a share of the burden in inverse ratio to the Japanese.
transcriber_notes: Rows: 9 as printed (3 blocks x 3 years). Row label printed once per block, blank on later rows.
Totals check: Japanese+Korean+Foreign = Total reconciles for all 6 population and tax rows; per-household rows not additive.

title: [Public Schools for Koreans: Schools, Expenditure, School Tax and Burden per Household, 1918-1923]
caption_extra: [Section: Management of Public Schools for Koreans] Untitled table. Expenditure and School Tax printed in 1,000 yen; average burden in yen.
context: Shows the growth, 1918-1923, of public schools for Korean children and of their expenditure, school tax and average burden per household, following the account of the 1919 programme of new schools.
transcriber_notes: Rows: 4 as printed. Table begins at top of p0204 (p0203 ends in prose). No totals printed.
The unit label above School Tax figures is not printed separately; taken as 1,000 Yen as for Expenditure (the printed 1,000 Yen label sits above the Expenditure row only).

title: [School Associations: Number, Population, Budget and Burden per Household, 1918-1923]
caption_extra: [Section: School Associations] Untitled table introduced by "as will be seen in the table below". Budget and burden in yen.
context: Shows the rise in the number, membership, budget and per-household burden of school associations (Japanese public education) since 1918, illustrating the swelling of their accounts since 1920.
transcriber_notes: Rows: 6 as printed. 1923 burden printed '25,33' (comma) -- kept as printed, probably a misprint for 25.33.
No totals printed.

title: Geographical Place Names
context: Appendix list giving the Japanese and Korean forms of the names of the provinces, provincial capitals, seaports, towns, mountains, rivers, islands and bays, for readers of the report.
transcriber_notes: Two side-by-side columns pairs read as one continuous list (left pair first, then right pair; the right pair begins with Junten at the top, continuing 'Other Towns').
Rows: 77 including 8 sub-heading rows (Provinces., Provincial Capitals, Principal Seaports., Other Towns, Principal Mountains., Principal Rivers., Principal Islands., Principal Bays.), 69 place rows.

Ditto marks '„' after Pyŏng-an etc. kept as printed in the Korean cell. Shin-gishū appears under both Capitals and Seaports as printed. Parenthetical alternatives (Seoul, Chemulpo, Songdo, Yalu, Tumen, Quelpart) are printed in the same line. Italic type in original.
No unreadable cells.
